items.title: Five Lessons From Cannes Lions 2026 Every Marketer Should Know - BW Marketing World
items.raw_summary: Every edition of Cannes Lions reflected where the advertising industry stood at a particular moment. This year, the conversations extended far beyond who won the most Lions. Across jury rooms, keynote sessions and award-winning work, a set of broader patterns emerged that pointed to where creativity, media and marketing were headed next.From AI becoming a practical business tool to a renewed emphasis on long-term brand building, Cannes Lions 2026 signalled that the industry had entered a more mature phase, one where effectiveness, context and trust were increasingly valued alongside creativity.Brand Building WinsOne of the strongest themes across the festival was the renewed focus on building brands rather than chasing momentary attention.Instead of rewarding one-off campaigns or ideas created purely to generate buzz, much of the work that stood out focused on solving real consumer problems, participating meaningfully in culture and reinforcing brand identity.The conversations across the festival suggested that creativity was increasingly being evaluated through its ability to create long-term business value rather than simply delivering short-term visibility.AI Gets PracticalUnlike previous years, where AI dominated conversations as an emerging technology, Cannes Lions 2026 reflected a more practical outlook.Brands, agencies and publishers focused less on whether to adopt AI and more on how to integrate it responsibly across creative development, media planning, measurement and production. Discussions centred on using AI to improve efficiency while ensuring that human insight, originality and strategic thinking remained central to creative work.Rather than replacing creativity, AI was increasingly viewed as an accelerator for it.Context Over IdentityAs privacy regulations continued to reshape digital advertising, marketers increasingly shifted from identity-based targeting towards understanding context, intent and consumer moments.Across discussions at Cannes Lions, contextual relevance emerged as one of the defining themes. Advertisers placed greater importance on reaching consumers based on what they were doing, feeling or consuming rather than relying solely on personal identifiers.This shift also encouraged publishers to develop AI-powered solutions that improved monetisation without depending on third-party identity data.Premium Media MattersWith AI-generated content flooding digital platforms, premium media environments have become increasingly valuable.Brands placed greater emphasis on trusted publishers, high-quality editorial environments and professionally curated content where attention was more meaningful and brand safety was stronger.The conversation around attention also evolved from simply measuring impressions to understanding engagement quality and consumer receptiveness.Authenticity Under ScrutinyAlongside the celebration of creative excellence, another debate continued to gain momentum at Cannes: the growing number of campaigns designed primarily for award recognition rather than genuine business impact.While some industry observers felt there had been an increasing trend of ads being created for awards and fewer actual brand campaigns over the years, others believed Cannes Lions 2026 marked a return to the fundamentals of brand building. According to them, the work that stood out was not built on one-off stunts but on strong brand identities, real consumer problems and meaningful cultural relevance. They also saw this as an important takeaway for India, where combining creative ingenuity with sustained brand thinking could strengthen its position on the global stage.Together, these perspectives suggested that while questions around award-focused work persisted, the conversation increasingly shifted towards creativity that delivered lasting value for brands.Beyond Metal CountsFor India, perhaps the biggest learning from Cannes Lions 2026 was that sustained brand thinking mattered as much as breakthrough ideas.Indian agencies continued to demonstrate exceptional cultural insight and creative ingenuity. However, the campaigns that resonated globally that year were those that combined creativity with consistency, long-term brand strategy and measurable business relevance.As global judging standards continued to evolve, India's next opportunity appeared to lie not simply in producing more award-winning campaigns, but in building brands whose creativity compounded over time.Cannes Lions 2026 made one thing clear: the future of advertising would be shaped not by the loudest ideas, but by the most meaningful ones. AI, contextual relevance, trusted media and long-term brand building were no longer separate conversations; they had become increasingly interconnected. As the industry adapted to new technologies and changing consumer expectations, creativity was redefined as a strategic capability that delivered enduring value rather than fleeting attention.

items.title: Sociedade médica repensa a sua comunicação com o público. Luís Maco (Sociedade Portuguesa de Gastrenterologia) revela que o objetivo é "travar desinformação" - Marketeer
items.raw_summary: A comunicação em saúde raramente vive de simplificações. Entre a necessidade de rigor científico e o desafio de chegar à população em geral, o equilíbrio tende a ser delicado. É nesse cruzamento que surge a campanha “A Saúde Digestiva não joga com Mitos”, explica Luís Maco, diretor-geral e financeiro da Sociedade Portuguesa de Gastrenterologia.
